interview.name: Uli
interview.answer: It’s on Sunday at the community center.

reflections: Mina and Uli interact with practical, supportive reciprocity; Mina offers help, and Uli responds by clarifying needs and limits.
Leo frames the request around immediate, concrete contributions, which helps Uli commit without overpromising.
Uli prefers simple, bounded commitments and benefits from clear specifics about what is most needed, when, and where.
Mina and Mara are both offering practical help and taking on clear task ownership around the repair drive.
Uli is cooperative but has limited capacity, so they benefit from explicit prioritization and simple, concrete requests.
Leo appears to be coordinating immediate needs by identifying the most useful support: tools, spare hands, and clear logistics.
Uli is a practical, low-bandwidth helper who keeps commitments modest and concrete.
Mina, Leo, Mara, and Jules coordinate by assigning specific tasks and setting aside needed materials, which keeps the group organized.
The repair effort is collaborative and time-bound, with attention to priorities like small fixes, spare parts, and the school pickup window.
Uli is dependable and willing to adapt his schedule to help with practical repairs.
Mara, Jules, Rosa, and Faye coordinate by sharing timing, lists, and updates so Uli can be effective.
The group is organizing around school pickup and a community-center repair drive, with clear preference for small fixes and spare-parts tasks.
Uli is cooperative and low-friction, repeatedly offering help with small fixes and tool jobs while waiting for details.
Faye, Vik, and Tess are all managing uncertain timing and logistics by promising to follow up once windows, plans, or final details are set.
The group relies on clear, incremental handoffs: one person gathers the list or lineup, and Uli responds by planning around it and showing up prepared.

events.text: Mina: How’s the repair drive going, Uli? Do you need a hand with anything?
events.speaker: Mina

events.text: Uli: It’s going, thanks for asking. I could use help sorting a few things, if you’ve got a moment.
events.speaker: Uli

events.text: Mina: Sure — what do you want me to sort first?
events.speaker: Mina

events.text: Uli: I can help with the repair drive, but I need to keep it simple today. If you tell me what’s most needed, I’ll do what I can.
events.speaker: Uli

events.text: Leo: Thanks, Uli — the biggest help is tools and a few spare hands. If you can just bring what you have, that’ll be great.
events.speaker: Leo

events.text: Uli: I can bring a basic toolbox and show up for a few hours. Just let me know when and where to be.
events.speaker: Uli

events.text: Mara: Sounds good — I’ll keep sorting the donated items and set aside anything that needs tools or spare parts. Let me know what you want me to tackle next.
events.speaker: Mara

events.text: Uli: That sounds perfect, Mara — please set aside the tool jobs and any small fixes that need spare parts. I’ll bring my toolbox and help where I can for a few hours.
events.speaker: Uli

events.text: Mara: Great, Uli — I’ll set those tool jobs and small fixes aside for you. Thanks for bringing your toolbox and a few hours to help.
events.speaker: Mara

events.text: Uli: I’ll bring my toolbox and take the small fixes first, Jules. If you’ve got anything needing spare parts, set it aside for me.
events.speaker: Uli

events.text: Jules: Perfect, Uli — I’ll set aside anything that needs spare parts and keep the small fixes ready for you. We’re still lining things up around the school pickup window, so your toolbox will help a lot.
events.speaker: Jules

events.text: Uli: That works for me — I’ll swing by after the school pickup window and start with the small fixes. Just point me to the spare-parts pile when I get there.
events.speaker: Uli

events.text: Rosa: Thanks, Uli — I’ve got the repair drive moved to Sunday at the community center, and I’ll keep everyone posted on what’s still needed.
events.speaker: Rosa

prov.value: The repair drive is being held on Sunday at the community center.

events.text: Uli: Thanks, Rosa — Sunday at the community center works for me. Just let me know the small fixes and spare-parts jobs, and I’ll help where I can.
events.speaker: Uli

prov.value: The repair drive is being held on Sunday at the community center.

events.text: Rosa: Wonderful, Uli — I’ll send you the small fixes and spare-parts list as soon as I’ve got it sorted.
events.speaker: Rosa

events.text: Faye: Sounds good — I’ll check our pickup timing and send you the window as soon as I can.
events.speaker: Faye

events.text: Uli: Thanks, Faye — that helps a lot. Send the window when you can, and I’ll plan around the small fixes and tool jobs.
events.speaker: Uli

events.text: Faye: Absolutely — I’ll check our school pickup timing and send you the window as soon as I have it.
events.speaker: Faye

events.text: Vik: Not much yet — we’re still lining folks up for the repair drive, and I’ll repeat the full time and place once the details are set.
events.speaker: Vik

events.text: Uli: That’s fine — send me the small fixes and any spare-parts jobs when you can, and I’ll help where I’m able.
events.speaker: Uli

events.text: Vik: Absolutely — I’ll send the small-fixes list and any spare-parts jobs as soon as I’ve got them, and I’ll repeat the full repair-drive plan once the details are set.
events.speaker: Vik

events.text: Uli: I can take the small fixes and any spare-parts jobs, Tess. Just point me to what needs doing most, and I’ll keep it simple.
events.speaker: Uli

events.text: Tess: Perfect — I’ll keep you on the small fixes and spare-parts jobs, and I’ll send the lineup as soon as the final time and place are set.
events.speaker: Tess

events.text: Uli: Thanks, Tess — that works for me. Just send the lineup when it’s ready, and I’ll be there with my toolbox.
events.speaker: Uli
